extraction.Name: Mary Dillon
extraction.Buyer: Chris Colome; consideration included a piano worth about $200.00, a team of horses, a set of harness and a buggy (the buggy and harness being used considerably, and the horses were small), food and clothing for five people over one winter (estimated at about $1000.00), two dozen chickens worth about 75 cents each, and $400 in cash
extraction.NOTES: Mary Dillon is the widow of William McClosky or Dillon (deceased February 17, 1924); she states the land was deeded to Chris Colome though records apparently show it was deeded to O'Hallern; she believed the land was worth at least $1000.00 more than received; Chris Colome promised to help her if in need but did not respond when asked after husband's death; document reference number 2331; witnesses mentioned: George Dillon, Tom Dillon, John, Ed, and Dave Colome
